title: A nonzero vector lies in a basis
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $V$ a $K$-vector space. Every $K$-linearly independent subset $S\subseteq V$ is contained in a $K$-basis of $V$, i.e. a subset $\mathcal B\supseteq S$ that is linearly independent over $K$ and spans $V$. In particular $V$ has a $K$-basis ($S=\emptyset$), and for every nonzero $v\in V$ there is a $K$-basis of $V$ containing $v$ ($S=\{v\}$, which is linearly independent since $cv=0$ with $c\neq0$ gives $v=c^{-1}cv=0$).

source.place: standard linear algebra (Zorn's lemma), used in the proof of lem-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-scalar-descent; Mathlib Module.Basis.extend
